eras.label: Elections under the Raj
eras.blurb: The Central Legislative Assembly elections of British India were contests on a franchise so narrow that under a tenth of adults could vote, with separate communal electorates. They still mattered: the Swaraj Party's entryism, Congress boycotts and returns, and the 1945–46 results that settled the mandate for Partition and the Constituent Assembly.

eras.label: The Nehru era
eras.blurb: The 1951–52 general election was the largest democratic exercise the world had attempted — a mostly illiterate electorate of 173 million choosing freely. Jawaharlal Nehru's Congress won three sweeping majorities on a divided opposition, setting the template of the one-party-dominant 'Congress system'.

eras.label: The Congress system tested
eras.blurb: The 1967 setback, Indira Gandhi's split of Congress and her 1971 'Garibi Hatao' landslide, the Emergency and the extraordinary Janata verdict of 1977 — the first time Congress lost power — then her 1980 return and Rajiv Gandhi's 1984 sympathy wave, still the largest majority in Indian history.

eras.label: Mandal, Mandir and the coalition era
eras.blurb: No single party won a majority in any of the five elections from 1989 to 1999. Caste and communal realignments — the Mandal report, the Ayodhya movement — broke the Congress system, lifted the BJP from two seats to power, and made the United Front and NDA coalitions the new normal.

eras.label: The UPA decade
eras.blurb: The 2004 upset ended 'India Shining' and brought Manmohan Singh to office at the head of the Congress-led UPA; 2009 renewed it with the best Congress result in two decades. Coalition management, the nuclear deal and rural welfare schemes defined the politics.

eras.label: The Modi era
eras.blurb: Narendra Modi's 2014 campaign delivered the first single-party majority since 1984 and reduced Congress to its lowest-ever tally; 2019 enlarged it. In 2024 the BJP fell short of a majority for the first time in a decade, governing through the NDA against a revived INDIA-bloc opposition.

The total electorate for the 1934 elections was 1,415,892 (from a population of 242 million), of which 1,135,899 were in contested constituencies. The total number of votes polled was 608,198.

General elections were held in British India in December 1945 to elect members of the Central Legislative Assembly and the Council of State. Election under Government of India Act 1935 were held with limited franchise and only around 10% of the population in direct British controlled provinces were eligible to vote based on their income and property.

In 1946, prior to the independence of India, members of the Constituent Assembly of India were selected through an indirect election by the elected legislators of the 1946 Indian provincial elections, conducted under the British government's Cabinet Mission plan.

General elections were held in India between 25 October 1951 and 21 February 1952, the first national elections after India gained independence in 1947. Voters elected 489 members of the first Lok Sabha, the lower house of the Parliament of India.

Under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru, the Indian National Congress easily won a second term in power, taking 371 of the 494 seats. They gained an extra seven seats (the size of the Lok Sabha had been increased by five) and their vote share increased from 45% to 48%.
Jawaharlal Nehru won another landslide victory in his third and final election campaign. The Indian National Congress received 44.7% of the vote and won 361 of the 494 elected seats.

General elections were held in India between 17 and 21 February 1967 to elect 520 of the 523 members of the fourth Lok Sabha, an increase of 15 from the previous session of Lok Sabha. Elections to State Assemblies were also held simultaneously, the last general election to do so.
General elections were held in India between 1 and 10 March 1971 to elect members of the fifth Lok Sabha. They were the fifth general elections since independence in 1947.

elections.summary: The elections resulted in a heavy defeat for the Indian National Congress (R), with the incumbent Prime Minister and INC(R) party leader Indira Gandhi losing her seat in Rae Bareli, while her son Sanjay lost his seat in Amethi. Morarji Desai of the Janata Party took office as the first non-Congress Prime Minister on 24 March.

The Janata Party alliance came into power in the 1977 general elections amidst public anger with the Indian National Congress (R) and the Emergency. However, its position was weak; the loose coalition barely held on to a majority with only 295 seats in the Lok Sabha and never quite had a firm grip on power.

elections.summary: General elections were held in India on 22 and 26 November 1989 to elect the members of the ninth Lok Sabha. The incumbent Indian National Congress (Indira) government under the premiership of Rajiv Gandhi lost its mandate, even though it was still the largest single party in the Lok Sabha.

The elections resulted in a hung parliament with no single party having a majority. The Bharatiya Janata Party, which had won the most seats despite finishing second in the popular vote, formed a short-lived government under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

elections.summary: General elections were held in India on 16, 22 and 28 February 1998 to elect the members of the twelfth Lok Sabha. The elections were held three years ahead of schedule after the government led by Inder Kumar Gujral collapsed when the Indian National Congress (INC) withdrew its support in November 1997.

The elections saw the National Democratic Alliance led by the Bharatiya Janata Party win a majority in the Lok Sabha, the first time since 1984 that a party or alliance had won an outright majority and the second since the 1977 elections that a non-Congress coalition had done so.
General elections were held in India in four phases between 20 April and 10 May 2004. Over 670 million people were eligible to vote, electing 543 members of the 14th Lok Sabha.

General elections were held in India in five phases between 16 April 2009 and 13 May 2009 to elect the members of the fifteenth Lok Sabha. With a registered electorate of 716 million and a turnout of 417 million voters, it was the largest democratic election in the world until being surpassed by the 2014 general election.

elections.summary: General elections were held in India in nine phases from 7 April to 12 May 2014 to elect the members of the 16th Lok Sabha. With 834 million registered voters, they were the largest-ever elections in the world until being surpassed by the 2019 election.
General elections were held in India in seven phases from 11 April to 19 May 2019 to elect the members of the 17th Lok Sabha. Votes were counted and the result was declared on 23 May.

General elections were held in India from 19 April to 1 June 2024 in seven phases, to elect all 543 members of the Lok Sabha. Votes were counted and the result was declared on 4 June to form the 18th Lok Sabha.
